_note: THE ODIN DEPLOYMENT CELL — the recipe for the bundle cut from a real trained network, CONV-FIRST, at S=16. MEASURED 2026-08-30, end to end, exit 0, deployed 0.9366 over the full test set on the DEFAULT core geometry (2 hard cores, one neural segment: core 0 at 127 logical axons / 254 physical rows / 120 neurons, core 1 at 121 / 242 / 10). WHY S=16 AND NOT S=4: S is DEPLOYMENT CONFIG, not a chip constraint, and S=4 was the whole 88% story. The same cell, changing only simulation_steps (with target_tq kept equal to it, the tier idiom and the domain rule's divisibility) deploys 0.8790 / 0.9129 / 0.9366 at S = 4 / 8 / 16 — +5.8 pp for a two-key edit, with the LIF-adaptation stage carrying it (0.8552 / 0.9113 / 0.9397). Both A6 pre-flight gauges said so before a single step ran: at levels=4 the VALUE gauge read FAIL (stem_0_full starved — its sample median 0.129 sits at 0.19 of the 2.65/4 grid step), and the TEMPORAL gauge reads a chain first-fire delay of 4.81 cycles that barely moves with S (4.73 / 4.88 / 4.96 at S = 8 / 16 / 32), so the delay/window ratio is 1.20 / 0.59 / 0.31 / 0.16 — only S=4 starts with its deepest hop firing after the window has closed. That 1.20 read PASS under the old 2x recovery bar; the bar is now the window itself. WHY NOT S=32: the T-anneal entry probe and the full-transform probe landed within one SE of each other (0.7730 vs 0.7779), so tuning_lossless_entry_fast_path declared a transform that cost 0.9823 -> 0.7730 'lossless at entry' and SKIPPED the whole ladder. The predicate compares two post-damage reads, so it cannot see damage; that is a filed flow defect, not an S=32 result. WHY NOT A WIDER VEHICLE: measured. 22 pretrain-only screens; the per-event twin folds a hop only when its effective weight spans its WHOLE input, so every narrow_conv with body_blocks >= 1 is refused by SLOT COUNT (a 3x3 conv over a 14x14 map feeds 2744 slots into a 126-slot weight), which rules out every candidate that reached 0.99 pretrain (0.9902-0.9910). The best FEASIBLE vehicle is a k27/s10 stem with trunk_width=126, trunk_blocks=2 at 0.9884 pretrain, and it runs the flow better than this one (LIF 0.9687 vs 0.9397, WQ cost 0.0000) — but ODIN's 127 count-currency ceiling refuses it at BOTH S: 129 events in one cycle at S=16 (lif_serial_fold) and a 134-per-window static bound at S=8 (odin export feasibility). Its 3-core mapping is otherwise clean and parity-exact. Depth x fan-in x S is bounded by that ceiling; this 2-hop vehicle is inside it. THE LADDER, RE-MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-08-30 (the numbers above came from a run that STARTED 14:12:08, seven minutes before the hop-0 STE commit 3a6fdfca they are filed under, so they are pre-STE reads): pretrain 0.9820, AQ 0.9820, LIF 0.9487, WQ at wb=4 0.9329, QV 0.9329, NF 0.9328, SCM 0.9328 with NF<->SCM streamed EXACT (torch.equal, atol=0), HCM 0.9340, nevresim probe 0.96 (25 samples), spike-count certificate exact=1.0 max|dcount|=0 over 20 neuron-windows. DEPLOYED IS 0.9340, not the 0.9366 above: the post-STE code reproduces 0.9340 twice (steS16 on 2026-08-30 and this HEAD run, same seed), so 0.9366 is the pre-STE outlier and 0.9340 is this cell's number.
